contract: `encoded` is the single `{key}` path segment in the reference form (spec rule 1); `decoded` is the key the server sees after its single percent-decode and equals `key` in every transmittable row (spec rules 3-4). Rows with `reject: true` are the reserved segments of spec rule 2 (`.`, `..`, `health`, `ttl`, `lock`): a conformant client raises before building the URL, so `encoded` and `decoded` are null. `encoded_alternates` lists the `encodeURIComponent` form (`! * ' ( )` raw) where it differs from `encoded`, and is absent otherwise; reject rows carry none. An SDK conforms when its encoding of `key` is in `[encoded] + encoded_alternates` (a missing `encoded_alternates` is `[]`).

vectors.note: Canonical 7-segment auto-mode key (test-vectors/cache-keys.json `single_integer`). Only `:` is encoded; identical bytes from all three reference encoders.
Embedded traversal: every `/` is `%2F`, so no `../` boundary exists for a URL parser to collapse. Server decodes once, then rejects (`/` outside charset; `..` substring).
Traversal aimed at the `/v1/cache/health` route token; inert once `/` is `%2F`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Query/fragment injection: `?` and `#` MUST be encoded or the client's URL parser truncates the key and emits a query string. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
Space is `%20` in a path segment, never `+` (form-encoding, which the server does not decode). Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
A literal `%` is encoded exactly once; the server decodes once and sees `100%`, then rejects it (charset). `%2525` would decode to `100%25`, a different key.
Dot segment: the plain encoding `.` is removed by every URL parser, and `%2E` is collapsed by the server's WHATWG parse (`/v1/cache/%2E` → `/v1/cache/`). No wire form reaches the validator.
Dot segment: unencoded, `/v1/cache/..` collapses to `/v1/` and `/v1/cache/../ttl` to `/v1/ttl`; `%2E%2E` is collapsed the same way by the server's WHATWG parse. No wire form reaches the validator.
Route token: `/v1/cache/health` is the health endpoint, so a GET for this key would return the health payload as a cache hit.
Route token: a final `ttl` segment selects the TTL sub-resource, so `/v1/cache/ttl` is read as an empty key plus `/ttl`.
Route token: a final `lock` segment selects the lock sub-resource, so `/v1/cache/lock` is read as an empty key plus `/lock`.
Trailing dots but NOT an all-dot segment: not a dot segment under either parsing model, so the dots stay raw. Server rejects the decoded `..` substring.
Leading dots, not an all-dot segment: sent verbatim (all characters unreserved). Server rejects the decoded `..` substring.

`:` → `%3A`, decoded once server-side. The server then rejects it: a key starting `ns:` must be `ns:{namespace}:{rest}` with a non-empty `{rest}` (spec/cache-key-format.md § Server-Side Requirements, Namespace), and this one has no `{rest}`.

Encoder-variance row (spec rule 4): `quote(safe="")` and `urlencoding::encode` produce `encoded`; `encodeURIComponent` produces the alternate. Both decode to `key`. Server rejects the decoded key (charset).
